requirement_text: IELTS Academic (paper or computer; IELTS Academic Online, IELTS General Training, IELTS Indicator and IELTS One Skill Retake NOT accepted): score equivalency table — IELTS 6.0 = TOEFL iBT 80 (component 20 old scale / 4.0 new scale) = Cambridge C1 Advanced/C2 Proficiency 169; IELTS 6.5 = TOEFL 90 (22/4.5) = CAE/CPE 176-180; IELTS 7.0 = TOEFL 100 (25/5.0) = CAE/CPE 185; IELTS 7.5 = TOEFL 113 (27/5.5) = CAE/CPE 191. "You can find minimum test scores in the relevant programme descriptions." Results may not be more than two years old and must be obtained in one single test.
limitations: Leiden does NOT publish one university-wide minimum — the equivalency table converts between test systems, but which row a given programme requires is set on that programme's own page. TOEFL scores from tests taken on or after 21 January 2026 show the overall score on the old 0-120 scale and component scores on the new 1-6 scale; the table above mixes the two scales for that reason, per the source document's own instruction.
researcher_notes: Read from the official 3-page PDF ("Last updated: February 2026"), not a summary — WebFetch's first attempt on this same PDF failed to parse it at all, so the numbers here came from reading the extracted document directly.
test_scale: IELTS Academic 0-9; TOEFL iBT old 0-120 and new 1-6 scales; Cambridge Scale ~142-230

requirement_text: Exemptions from the English test requirement: holders of an IB Diploma taught in English or with English A HL; secondary or higher education completed in the USA, UK, Ireland, New Zealand, Australia, Canada (except French-taught programmes), Singapore, South Africa or Malta; a German Abitur with English at least at Grundkurs level in the final year; certain other diplomas per Leiden's own diploma requirements list.
limitations: "In exceptional cases, students who otherwise qualify for an exemption but whose application documents cast doubt on their English proficiency, may be asked to sit an English exam."

requirement_text: International Baccalaureate: "Most degree courses offered at Bristol require a point score of at least 32 with some requirements as high as 40 points, with 18 points at Higher Level."
limitations: A range across programmes (32-40 points), not a single threshold. This page did not state IELTS/TOEFL scores.
researcher_notes: "grade requirements for International A-levels are the same as for UK A-levels" per the same research pass, though not captured on this specific page as a verbatim quote.
test_scale: IB Diploma total 45 points; Higher Level subject grades 1-7

requirement_text: Language Profile B — IELTS Academic: undergraduate "7.0 overall with 7.0 in writing and 6.5 in all other skills". TOEFL iBT for tests taken up to 20 January 2026: undergraduate "95 overall with R22, L21, S23, W24"; for tests taken from 21 January 2026: undergraduate "5 overall, 5 in writing and 4.5 in all other skills".
limitations: Bristol assigns each course one of nine language profiles (A-H plus an International Programme profile); Profile B is recorded here as one illustrative profile, not the university-wide requirement. Which profile applies to a given course is stated on that course's own page.
researcher_notes: Test results must be obtained within two years of the programme start date, and component scores must come from a single sitting (no combining certificates), per the profile overview page.
test_scale: IELTS Academic 0-9; TOEFL iBT on both the 0-120 and post-21-January-2026 banded scales

requirement_text: "YOS exam will NOT be held and NOT accepted." International undergraduate applicants are instead evaluated on the accepted diploma and standardized-exam equivalency list published by the International Students Unit.
limitations: The page itself is marked "update: 29.05.2023" even though the site's own navigation elsewhere shows undergraduate rules "Updated on 25th of June 2026" — the YÖS-not-accepted statement was not independently re-confirmed on a page dated within this pass. Confidence set to medium for that reason, not high.
researcher_notes: A real negative result worth recording rather than assuming: several other Turkish universities in this same pass (Gebze) DO list TR-YÖS as an accepted route, so this is genuinely Yıldız-specific, not a national rule.

requirement_text: "Who Can Apply? (Undergraduate)" — eligible applicant categories: (1) purely foreign nationals who have not received education in or graduated from high schools in Türkiye (excluding embassy/international schools within the MOBİS system); (2) Blue Card holders and former Turkish citizens who renounced Turkish citizenship, provided they have not been educated in Türkiye or the TRNC; (3) naturalized T.C. citizens born as foreign nationals, provided they have not been educated in Türkiye or the TRNC; (4) T.C. citizens who completed secondary education entirely abroad (excluding the TRNC), including at MEB schools abroad; (5) TRNC citizens who completed high school in the TRNC and hold GCE AL results, or completed high school entirely abroad and hold a TR-YÖS result. "In Summary: As of 2026, if you have received even a part of your high school education at a standard high school in Türkiye or the TRNC, your application will not be accepted, even if you are a foreign national or a Blue Card holder."
researcher_notes: Read directly from the university's own page after expanding its collapsed accordion sections in the browser — a first WebFetch attempt at this same URL returned specific TOEFL/PTE/Cambridge scores (78, 67, etc.) that do NOT appear anywhere on the real page; that response was discarded as unreliable rather than recorded. Worth flagging for anyone reviewing this batch: always re-verify a WebFetch summary against the page's own rendered text before trusting specific numbers.

requirement_text: "The minimum TOL score for admission, rounded to the nearest whole number, must be equal to or greater than 30/100 (thirty) points." Accepted alternatives to the TOL, converted to a comparable hundredths score: TOLC-I (CISIA, administered in Italian), CEnT-S (CISIA, administered in English), and SAT (College Board).
limitations: Scoped to Engineering Bachelor programmes specifically — Politecnico di Milano also offers non-Engineering bachelor's programmes (e.g. Architecture, Design) admitted under separate calls not covered by this document. The PDF itself states: "ATTENTION: the English translation... is only an information aid addressed to international students. From a normative point of view, the Italian version is the one to be considered."
researcher_notes: Official "Call for Applications for the Engineering Bachelor degree programmes... for the 2026/2027 academic year", fetched as a PDF directly (WebFetch's URL tool refused to parse it; retrieved via direct download and read as a document instead).

requirement_text: Candidates are not required to separately demonstrate English proficiency if they: "have taken a TOL or TOLC-I and have answered at least 24 correct questions in the English section"; or "have taken a CENTS test or a SAT test with a score equivalent to a TOL score greater than or equal to 30/100". Students who do not demonstrate English proficiency are assigned an "English OFA" (Additional Educational Obligation) which prohibits adding extra courses, adding courses from later years, or submitting an independent study plan until resolved.
scope: Engineering Bachelor programmes — English proficiency / OFA
limitations: Scoped to Engineering Bachelor programmes per the same call.
researcher_notes: The OFA consequence is the practically important part for a student — passing the entrance test alone does not resolve the English requirement.
